issues.body: `_obs_lane_rows` announces an invalid lane container, name, or row, but it still silently accepts malformed data below that row. A non-object `1h`/`24h` value becomes `None` without a diagnostic, and each invalid/missing/negative `success`, `failure`, or `defer` value is converted to `0` by `_obs_count(...) or 0`. For example, `{'worker': {'1h': {'success': 'many', 'failure': -1, 'defer': null}}}` publishes a worker lane with all three counts at zero and prints no warning. That is precisely the false-healthy presentation the new announced-drop contract says it prevents. The added lane cases test only an invalid whole row and a fully valid row, so deleting diagnostics/validation for nested lane measurements remains outside the evidence path.
issues.fix_hint: Validate each present lane window and each counter with an independently bounded lane-seam drop log before defaulting absent values. Announce present-but-unreadable windows/counters while preserving the intended policy for genuinely absent fields. Add literal-input/literal-expected self-test cases for malformed window containers and malformed/negative counters, plus a valid silent control, so each guard's wrong answer turns a named check red.
issues.title: Malformed lane windows and counters still fail open as healthy data

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The change makes several top-level observability shape losses visible, but the lane seam still silently converts malformed nested measurements into healthy-looking zeros. Because the new tests cover only the lane container/name/row guards, they do not establish the stated every-drop-announced contract for the data that actually supplies lane health. This is a major, non-vacuity/completeness gap in the marquee behavior.
